topics.title: Structured bindings unpack a pair
topics.body: One declaration names both halves of a pair or tuple, which removes the `first`/`second` noise from loops.

topics.title: auto drops top-level const
topics.body: Deduction copies the value and discards the top-level qualifier, so `auto` from a const int gives an int; `const auto&` keeps it.

topics.title: nullptr replaces NULL
topics.body: It has its own type and converts to any pointer without being mistaken for the integer zero by an overload.

topics.title: if constexpr selects at compile time
topics.body: The false branch is discarded during instantiation, so it can contain code that would not compile for that type.

topics.title: optional avoids a sentinel
topics.body: The type states that a value may be absent, so no legal value has to be reserved as "not found".

topics.title: Linear search scans every element
topics.body: It stops at the first match and is the only option when the data is unsorted; worst case is one pass.

topics.title: Selection sort picks the minimum each pass
topics.body: It scans the unsorted tail for the smallest value and swaps it into place, which is O(n²) but uses no extra memory.

topics.title: Merging two sorted ranges is linear
topics.body: Two pointers advance through the inputs, always taking the smaller head, which is the combine step of merge sort.

topics.title: A stack is last in, first out
topics.body: The most recent push is the first pop, which is why stacks model undo, recursion and expression evaluation.

topics.title: A queue is first in, first out
topics.body: The earliest push leaves first, which is the shape of scheduling and breadth-first traversal.

topics.title: A hash map trades order for speed
topics.body: Average lookup is constant and keys are unordered, which is the right trade when only membership matters.

topics.title: detach lets a thread run independently
topics.body: A detached thread owns itself and cannot be joined; the program must not exit while it still reads shared state.

topics.title: lock_guard releases at scope exit
topics.body: The mutex is unlocked by the guard’s destructor, so an early return or exception cannot leave it locked.

topics.title: A condition_variable waits for a signal
topics.body: The waiter releases the lock while asleep and reacquires it before returning, which avoids burning a core.

topics.title: atomic load reads one snapshot
topics.body: A relaxed load returns the current value without a lock, which is enough for a single counter.

topics.title: async returns a future
topics.body: The task runs on another thread and `get()` blocks until its result is ready, propagating any exception.

topics.title: A data race is undefined behaviour
topics.body: Two unsynchronised accesses with one write are not merely unpredictable; the standard says nothing about the result, so the fix is synchronisation, not testing.

topics.title: A header guard prevents double inclusion
topics.body: The `#ifndef`/`#define` pair makes the second inclusion a no-op, which is why a header can be included from several files.

topics.title: Assertions document an invariant
topics.body: The check runs in debug builds and disappears with `NDEBUG`, so it documents an invariant without costing release performance.

topics.title: Sanitizers catch memory bugs
topics.body: Compiling with `-fsanitize=address` reports an out-of-bounds access at the point it happens; the flag is a build decision, not a code change.

topics.title: A unit test pins behaviour
topics.body: A test states the expected result and fails loudly when the implementation drifts, which is cheaper than a manual check.

topics.title: A commit records one change
topics.body: A small, reviewable commit with a message that states the intent is what makes history useful later.

topics.title: A factory hides the concrete type
topics.body: The caller asks for a shape and receives a base pointer, so adding a new shape does not touch the call site.

topics.title: An observer is notified by its subject
topics.body: The subject keeps a list of listeners and calls each one when its state changes, which decouples the two sides.

topics.title: A strategy is a swappable algorithm
topics.body: The behaviour is injected as a callable, so the caller can change the algorithm without editing the class.

topics.title: A builder assembles step by step
topics.body: The builder collects the parts and produces the finished object once, which keeps the constructor from taking ten arguments.

topics.title: An adapter fits an old interface
topics.body: It translates one interface into the one the caller expects, so old code can be reused without rewriting it.

topics.title: A singleton owns its only instance
topics.body: The instance is a function-local static, which is created on first use and destroyed at exit.

topics.title: SOLID keeps a class focused
topics.body: A class with one reason to change is easier to test; the report below formats, while the caller decides where it goes.
